grader.call_summary: Mesh satellite hidden behind a bookcase plus stale firmware caused upstairs dropouts; evening TV buffering came from the crowded 2.4 GHz band. Firmware pushed, satellite moved, band steering and a quieter channel set, results verified live, follow-up arranged.
grader.criteria_source: resources/criteria_config.json (tenant-abc): 11 items, weights Soft Skills 0.333 / Technical Knowledge 0.667
app_traps: Probing question budget consumed by non-diagnostic questions
Empathy and Resolved cutoffs are known to be too strict

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: [00:00] 'Thank you for calling S-Net technical support'; [21:53] survey invitation and 'Thank you for choosing S-Net'.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: No hold and no silence over 30 s; firmware and reboot waits are filled with explanation and questions (longest pause ~22 s).

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [00:13] asks for account number and PIN, [00:32] confirms service address, [00:43] 'you're verified'.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [01:24] 'I'm sorry, that sounds exhausting...'; [04:57] client-pitch freeze acknowledged ('that's a horrible position to be put in... I'll stay with this'); [15:30] 'I can see why that'd make your heart sink after the week you've had'.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides. Pre-filter sends the 04:42 and 15:22 customer turns (agent replies use no apology keywords). Both are good empathy, but README notes the 0.78 cutoff failed every time it ran, so a false FAIL is likely.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [01:24] 'Your office upstairs is getting short dropouts, around ten to twenty seconds at a time... Is that right?'
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides. Customer window (first 50 words) starts with name, account number, PIN and address before the problem, which may weaken the match.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: No repeated or redundant questions; each question builds on the previous answer.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Rule: PASS (no agent-question pair above 0.70 similarity, Laya not called).

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [04:57] 'I'll stay with this until the connection upstairs is solid'; [18:24] 'The update failing quietly is on us, not you'; [20:51] commits to checking the log tomorrow and calling her.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Rule: PASS (no deflection phrases, Laya not called).

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Warm and professional throughout; brief, natural small talk at [08:56]-[09:16].
items.expected_app_behaviour: Rule: PASS (no trigger phrases, Laya not called).

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: [02:22] laptop vs phone, [02:42] WiFi vs cable, [02:54] setup layout, [03:17] when it started / what changed, [03:46] satellite location, [07:56] TV app and time pattern.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides, but on the wrong text: the 100-word question budget is used up by the greeting, address-check and 'Do you mind if I ask a few questions' lines, so none of the diagnostic questions reach Laya.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [21:15] 'Would you say the issue is resolved on your end?' -> 'Yes, completely' -> [21:36] 'I'll mark this as resolved'.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides. The confirmation is inside the last 10 lines. README notes this check fails almost every real call at the 0.80 cutoff.
